correctness.rationale: Every rational line is parametrized by [s:t] and its two defining restrictions are λΔ and ℓΔ for Δ=s^q t-s t^q. Geometric integrality excludes both zero; this gives reduced (q+1)-point or uniquely doubled rational (q+2)-point schemes and excludes all nonrational points on rational lines. The degree-(q+1) ideal of all projective rational points consists of alternating Frobenius minors. Degeneracy of its alternating matrix would force zero differential on C at a rational radical point, contradicting smooth complete intersection. Thus the containing surface is a smooth symplectic Frobenius surface; tangent directions are isotropic. The uniquely doubled point on each isotropic line makes the tangent map bijective. Distinct quadratic conjugates span a rational line, so no degree-two points occur. Genus and two initial zeta coefficients follow from adjunction and Newton identities. Both sample finite-field scripts passed independently and are not relied upon for the universal proof.
